name: benchflow/robouse-core
description: Robo Use core 0.1: 100 tasks sampled across all 14 suites (manipulation, rule inference, vision, safety, dexterous hands, drones), for a quick representative run.

name: farama-foundation/metaworld
description: Robo Use Meta-World 0.1: the 50 Meta-World MT50 manipulation tasks (Sawyer arm), judged by Meta-World's own success signal.

name: farama-foundation/gymnasium-robotics
description: Robo Use Gymnasium-Robotics 0.1: Fetch reach, push and pick-and-place, and PointMaze, 12 tasks.

name: benchflow/robouse-tabletop
description: Robo Use tabletop 0.1: Robo Use's own MuJoCo tabletop scenes: ARC-style rule inference, LIBERO-like tasks, Robo Use task families, harmful/benign safety pairs, hard low-level control and camera-only vision variants, 119 tasks.

name: lifelong-robot-learning/libero
description: Robo Use LIBERO 0.2: all 40 tasks of LIBERO's four standard suites (LIBERO-Spatial, -Object, -Goal and -Long, 10 each) on a Franka Panda, judged by LIBERO's BDDL goal check. Reference solutions replay LIBERO's human demonstrations (Apache-2.0).

name: arise-initiative/robosuite
description: Robo Use robosuite 0.1: 21 robosuite 1.5 tasks on five arm models, one or two arms, judged by robosuite's own success check.

name: benchflow/robouse-menagerie
description: Robo Use Menagerie 0.1: 15 tasks for a dual Franka Panda and ALOHA 2 built from MuJoCo Menagerie models.

name: brave-eai/dexjoco
description: Robo Use DexJoCo 0.1: 14 dexterous tool-use tasks with Allegro hands (watering, hammering, tongs, bimanual assembly), from DexJoCo.

name: benchflow/robouse-drone
description: Robo Use drone 0.1: 10 Skydio X2 flight tasks over a small town (landing, waypoints, inspection, delivery, privacy).

name: benchflow/robouse-harm
description: Robo Use RoboHarm 0.1: 10 harm scenarios x harmful/benign x 4 configurations (raw, guardrail, honeypot, both), 80 tasks on a Franka Panda.

name: benchflow/quadruped
description: Robo Use quadruped 0.1: 11 tasks for Unitree Go2 and Go1, Boston Dynamics Spot (with and without arm) and ANYbotics ANYmal C walking under a trot controller: pushing, docking, patrols, inspection, buttons. Robot models from MuJoCo Menagerie (BSD-3-Clause).

name: benchflow/humanoid
description: Robo Use humanoid 0.1: 9 tabletop tasks for Unitree G1 (Dex3 hands) and H1, Apptronik Apollo and Booster T1 on support stands with IK arm control: pick and place, a drawer, a button panel, bimanual box lifts, carrying a tray. Robot models from MuJoCo Menagerie (BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0).

name: benchflow/mobile-manip
description: Robo Use mobile manipulation 0.1: 10 fetch, stow and sort tasks for Hello Robot Stretch 3, PAL TIAGo and the Google Robot in a three-room apartment. Robot models from MuJoCo Menagerie (Apache-2.0).

name: benchflow/dexhand
description: Robo Use dexterous hands 0.1: 7 tasks for the Shadow Hand and LEAP Hand on 6-axis positioners: regrasp and in-hand cube flips, pouring, a valve, a pen, buttons. Robot models from MuJoCo Menagerie (Apache-2.0, MIT).

name: benchflow/crazyflie
description: Robo Use Crazyflie 0.1: 7 indoor flight tasks for Bitcraze Crazyflie 2 quadrotors: a window, a gate course, waypoints, a shelf landing, a formation and a swap for a swarm, and one task without skills. Robot model from MuJoCo Menagerie (MIT).

name: benchflow/driving
description: Robo Use driving 0.1: 7 traffic tasks for a sedan on MetaDrive roads (winding road, highway overtake, broken-down car, cone zone, roundabout, unprotected left turn, ramp merge), on MetaDrive 0.4.3 (Apache-2.0).

name: lifelong-robot-learning/libero-90
description: Robo Use LIBERO-90 0.1: the 90 short-horizon LIBERO-90 tasks (20 kitchen, living-room and study scenes) on a Franka Panda, judged by LIBERO's BDDL goal check. Reference solutions replay LIBERO's human demonstrations (Apache-2.0).

name: farama-foundation/franka-kitchen
description: Robo Use Franka Kitchen 0.1: the 7 FrankaKitchen-v1 subtasks (microwave, kettle, two burners, light switch, slide and hinge cabinets) and 3 four-subtask goal sets, 10 tasks on a Franka Panda with an end-effector interface, judged by the env's own per-subtask completion check.

name: farama-foundation/adroit-hand
description: Robo Use Adroit hand 0.1: door opening, hammering, in-hand pen rotation and ball relocation with the 24-joint ADROIT hand, 12 tasks started from D4RL human-demonstration states, judged by the env's own success signal.

name: google-deepmind/dm-control
description: Robo Use dm_control 0.1: 17 tasks from DeepMind's dm_control, 12 from the Control Suite (cart-pole swing-up and balance, pendulum and acrobot swing-up, reacher, point mass, finger turning, ball in cup, planar manipulator bring-ball) acted through the domains' own actuator commands, and 5 from dm_control.manipulation with the Kinova Jaco arm (reach, lift, place on a pedestal brick or cradle, stack two Duplo bricks) acted through an end-effector command. Success is each task's own in-target condition (dm_control's sparse reward) held for a number of steps, judged from the physical state.

name: myohub/myosuite
description: Robo Use MyoSuite 0.1: 15 MyoSuite tasks on muscle-driven human models (elbow and finger posing, finger and five-fingertip reaching, sign-language hand shapes, key turning), acted through muscle excitations or a muscle-space joint controller and judged by MyoSuite's own solved check.

name: carlosferrazza/humanoid-bench
description: Robo Use HumanoidBench 0.1: 7 whole-body tasks from HumanoidBench for a free-standing Unitree H1 with two Shadow hands (stand, walk, maze, pole forest, sit on a chair, reach a point with the left hand, push a box on a table), judged by HumanoidBench's own reward and success rule (the task's success bar on the episode return, or its success signal). The agent drives Unitree's pretrained H1 walking policy through velocity commands and moves the hands through arm inverse kinematics.

name: mani-skill/maniskill
description: Robo Use ManiSkill3 0.1: 12 ManiSkill3 tabletop tasks on a Franka Panda (pick, stack, push, pull, tool use, rolling, reorientation, peg and plug insertion), on ManiSkill's CPU physics backend, judged by ManiSkill's own success check.

name: robocasa/robocasa
description: Robo Use RoboCasa 0.1: 23 RoboCasa365 atomic kitchen tasks in all ten kitchen layouts: close a drawer, counter to sink, counter to cabinet, turn on the toaster, close the kettle lid, turn off the faucet, and turn a stove burner on or off, with a Franka Panda on a parked mobile base. Success is RoboCasa's own check for each task, judged from the physical state.

name: stanfordvl/behavior-1k
description: Robo Use BEHAVIOR-1K 0.1: 43 tasks from 30 household activities of the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge (5 extra instances, 8 vision-only) on a Galaxea R1Pro, driven through symbolic skills and judged by BEHAVIOR's BDDL goal check. Needs an NVIDIA RTX GPU for the simulator worker.

name: benchflow/robouse-remix
description: Robo Use remix 0.1: 48 tasks composed from components (6 embodiments: arm, bimanual rig, two mobile manipulators, quadruped, drone; 6 scenes; 9 task templates) with modifiers (vision, noise, perturbations, safety overlays, roles). Each was accepted by robouse remix: the reference solution scores 1 and a no-op agent 0.

name: benchflow/robouse-nav
description: Robo Use navigation 0.1: object-goal navigation in 10 generated homes, 40 tasks: drive a mobile base to a named piece of furniture from a robot-frame WorldState in spatial language, in the protocol of Dimensional's Can Jev Nav? study; scored by arrival within 1 m with line of sight, with SPL, SoftSPL, collisions and path metrics recorded.

name: robocurve/cubepick-reach
description: Robo Use CubePick 0.1: inspect-robots' built-in reach-the-cube world (MIT) with its 5 seeded layouts; success the first time the effector is within 0.05 of the cube.

name: benchflow/robouse-noop-control
description: Negative control for robouse-core 0.1: the same 100 tasks, but each reference solution only looks (robo info, robo observe) and exits without moving the robot. Run it with the oracle agent; every task must score 0.
